annotation.title_clean: ASME Student Design Challenge; When Machines Decide: Ethical and Regulatory Challenges in Autonomous Robotic Governance
annotation.title_en: ASME Student Design Challenge; When Machines Decide: Ethical and Regulatory Challenges in Autonomous Robotic Governance
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra Online Archive (BS capstone thesis)
annotation.summary_en: Undergraduate capstone abstract combining a technical design of a waste-collection robot with an STS study of accountability gaps in autonomous robotics governance. It finds outdated human-centered liability models and reactive regulation, and argues for anticipatory governance, ethical oversight and rigorous design processes before deployment.
key_provisions_or_claims: Existing frameworks rely on outdated human-centered liability models that fail to apportion accountability among developers, operators and deployers.
Governance is largely reactive, with regulation following incidents.
Anticipatory governance, ethical oversight and structured development are needed before deployment.
Recommends embedding fail-safes and accountability tracking into engineering design.
Waste-collection robot prototype demonstrates mobility, collection and disposal in a model city.
